kaigo-gap-reserve-check.heading: Check emergency supplies for actual usability
paragraphs: Supplies inside a bag are not necessarily usable when needed. Check whether flashlights and radios have compatible batteries or power and actually work, using the facility’s inspection method. If the responsible worker does not know the storage location, retrieving them may take time.

Cash and necessary documents can support access to help or information during a disaster. Prepare and manage them according to the facility plan and assigned responsibilities; do not leave personal information or money freely accessible for anyone to take.

Needs differ individually. Check mobility equipment, hearing-aid supplies, routine care items and current medicines with the person and responsible worker. One shared bag does not establish that every individual need is met.

Alongside names and quantities, record why items are unusable, what is missing, who will replenish them and when to recheck. Expired or incompatible items are not usable reserves even if counted in stock. Report uninspected items separately as unconfirmed.

[Learning example] A radio is present, but its stored batteries are incompatible. Backup supplies for a hearing-aid user remain unchecked. Do not finish at “radio present”; hand over battery incompatibility separately from unknown personal supplies.

These examples do not prescribe identical types or quantities for all facilities. Match reserves to the response plan and personal needs. Confirm medicines with responsible staff or healthcare professionals; do not change types or quantities from this learning list alone.

kaigo-gap-body-direction.heading: Read right and left from the person’s body
paragraphs: Use the person’s own right and left for body descriptions. Facing them, their right appears on the worker’s left. Specify the reference, such as “the person’s right,” rather than only “this side.”

The ascending colon normally runs upward on the person’s right abdomen. The transverse colon crosses, followed by the descending colon downward on the left. Do not confuse diagram viewing direction with body-area names.

Compare the diagram with the route from the person’s lower right abdomen upward, across left and down the left. This practices anatomy relationships. Understanding arrows does not establish pressure, duration, repetitions or permission for abdominal procedures.

For abdominal pain or other concerns, record location, onset and the person’s words and communicate to healthcare professionals or the supervising instructor. Do not diagnose from diagram orientation or start applying abdominal pressure.

Pregnancy, inflammatory bowel disease, abdominal surgery or wounds are important conditions to convey when discussing support. These alone do not establish permission or prohibition; confirm a suitable response with professionals. This lesson teaches orientation and terms.

kaigo-gap-anatomy-terms.heading: Distinguish scrotum, testes and foreskin
paragraphs: The scrotum is the external sac surrounding the testes. Testes are glands within it. The outer sac and inner organs differ; do not use identical names when describing observed areas.

The foreskin covers the glans at the penis tip and differs from scrotum and testes. If instructions use unclear names, confirm which area and what action is intended. Similar-looking words do not justify applying the same movement.

Do not guess pulling direction or force while an explanation remains unclear. If the target is unknown, do not begin that unconfirmed movement; ask a supervising instructor or healthcare professional. With pain or resistance, stop forcing the action and report condition.

Respect modesty and privacy during consultation. Avoid unnecessary public exposure or disclosure to unrelated people. Tell necessary recipients the confirmed area, personal words and unknown content separately.

This lesson establishes names and the need not to turn unclear instructions into action. The original material’s male-cleaning movement has not been confirmed here as a safe technique. Confirm individual intimate-care procedures through professional instruction and facility methods.

kaigo-depth-qol-outcome.heading: Consider quality of life through personal experience
paragraphs: QOL means quality of life, including emotional fulfillment through satisfaction, happiness and purpose. Many completed staff tasks alone do not establish improvement in the person’s life.

When reviewing an activity, ask what it meant to the person as well as what was done and how often. Listen to comments such as “It was enjoyable” or “I had little chance to talk.” Do not substitute staff preferences or satisfaction for personal evaluation.

Performing movements independently differs from making choices. Someone needing hand-movement help may choose activity type, time and desired role. Assistance quantity alone does not establish satisfaction or wishes.

[Learning example] During photo sorting, the person says, “We sorted more, but I wanted time to talk about the memories.” Quantity and desired time are separate information. Ask again how they want to spend time and which parts to do together.

If an activity is unsuitable, record current wishes and difficult participation areas and tell the team. Do not increase activity counts merely to improve records. Review support through wishes, abilities and safety together.

Do not diagnose psychological condition or independently change the care plan from one reply or activity count. Practice checking personal experience and reporting it as information for reviewing support.

kaigo-depth-community-choice.heading: Support community participation with personal choice
paragraphs: Community and group participation requires opportunities to express wishes and choose involvement. Taking everyone to one place is insufficient if participation is unwanted or accessible methods are absent.

People receiving care can contribute through experience and strengths as well as receive support. Ask desired roles, not only what should be done for them. Needing assistance does not mean inability to contribute.

If participation methods do not fit, ask which parts are difficult. Discuss approaches and support that use wishes and abilities. Do not require one identical method or exclude someone because one part is difficult.

[Learning example] Someone enjoying recorded books wants to introduce one at a community gathering. Restricting presentations to independent print readers prevents sharing that experience. Ask how they want to present and discuss preparation and format.

This does not mean every activity suits everyone equally. Adjust actual participation through wishes, abilities, needed support, location and operating conditions. Consult the person and responsible worker rather than deciding the form from staff ideas alone.

kaigo-depth-service-location.heading: Distinguish services through location and use
paragraphs: To distinguish basic care services, identify where support occurs and who travels where. Separate home visits by workers, day attendance by the person and living in a residential facility.

Home help visits the person’s home. Day care supports attendance during daytime. Residential support accompanies living in the facility. Connect names with living location and how help is received rather than memorizing labels alone.

A transport vehicle or care-worker presence alone does not identify service type. Check support location, return home after use and whether the person lives there. Do not decide the whole from one clue.

One person’s needs may vary by period or time of day. In actual handoffs, organize confirmed person, date/time, place and support, separating undecided points. Service names alone do not finalize schedules.

This classification explains setting and provision, not individual eligibility, insurance benefits, fees or facility selection. For actual arrangements, ask wishes and consult responsible staff, care managers or other appropriate people.

kaigo-depth-care-evaluation.heading: Separate implemented support from goal achievement
paragraphs: A care plan connects desired life with specific goals and support. Staff tasks alone do not show the intended personal outcome. Check relationships between wishes, goals and help.

An implementation record shows whether planned action occurred. Responses and activity results inform progress toward goals. The number of staff prompts cannot directly prove personal goal achievement.

[Learning example] The goal is choosing an afternoon activity. Staff explained three times, but the person said, “I do not know what I can choose.” Three explanations are implementation facts. Without an understood choice, they do not establish achievement.

When results differ from expectations, review missing information, explanation and participation conditions, and goal suitability as a team. Do not assume insufficient personal effort; use words and observations as evidence.

Evaluation revisits suitable support rather than merely increasing scores or counts. Record actions, responses and unknowns separately and share with the person and responsible staff. Discuss actual goal or assistance changes rather than deciding alone.

162.title: Check emergency supplies for actual usability
objectives: Report individual unknowns in a way that supports replenishment and rechecking.
162.context: Learn emergency-supply inspection and handoff, not identical reserve types or quantities.
162.artCaption: Staff check supplies, distinguishing presence from usability when needed.

163.title: Read right and left from the person’s body
objectives: Explain colon relationships from personal right and left.
Separate anatomy understanding from decisions to perform techniques.
163.context: Practice body orientation separately from symptom assessment or massage training.
163.artCaption: Listen to the person and check sites. The image shows neither colon locations nor abdominal massage.

164.title: Distinguish scrotum, testes and foreskin
objectives: Clarify unknown actions without guessing and preserve dignity.
164.context: Learn names and clarification, not intimate-cleaning performance from text alone.
164.artCaption: Staff prepare clean supplies. The image cannot explain intimate washing or moving anatomical structures.

165.title: Consider quality of life through personal experience
objectives: Separate activity quantity from personal meaning and satisfaction.
Support choices despite assistance needs and use wishes to review care.
165.context: Practice evaluating outcomes beyond staff workload and ask what matters to the person.
165.artCaption: Listen while viewing photographs and check what the person values through their words.

166.title: Support community participation with personal choice
objectives: Respect choices and desired community roles.
Plan support together around difficult parts.
166.context: Consider choice, roles and access conditions beyond simply sharing a venue.
166.artCaption: Different people engage in activities. Seek individual participation rather than identical tools or methods.

167.title: Distinguish services through location and use
objectives: Distinguish home-visit, day and residential forms through support and living locations.
Separate category names from actual schedules and access conditions.
167.context: Learn basic provision, not insurance eligibility or facility suitability judgments.
167.artCaption: Home visits, attendance and residential living illustrate differences in setting and use.

168.title: Separate implemented support from goal achievement
objectives: Record staff actions separately from personal achievement.
Avoid assumed causes and arrange evaluation with the person and team.
168.context: Use specific information to distinguish implementation and evaluation rather than deciding from activity counts.
168.artCaption: Review records with the person, separating help from responses when revisiting the plan.

weekly-kaigo-gap-reserve-check-probe.prompt: A radio has incompatible batteries; hearing-aid backup supplies remain unchecked. Which handoff is appropriate?
options: Record radio and batteries as usable because the radio exists.
Record unchecked personal supplies as unnecessary.
Remove unusable items without assigning replacement or rechecking.
Separate incompatibility from unknown personal supplies and confirm replenishment roles and recheck plans.
rationales: Equipment without compatible power is not established as usable.
Unknown does not mean unnecessary; individual needs still require checking.
Removal alone does not restore usable reserves; arrange replenishment and follow-up.
This preserves confirmed incompatibility versus unchecked needs and assigns next checks.

weekly-kaigo-gap-body-direction-probe.prompt: A facing worker calls the abdomen on their own left “the person’s left.” Which correction is appropriate?
options: Change personal-side names according to worker position.
Use the person’s body: ascending colon normally right, descending left.
Avoid a reference and say only “this side.”
Knowing arrows confirms permission to touch the abdomen.
rationales: The person’s body defines sides, not the worker’s stance.
Facing reverses visual sides; this uses personal anatomy.
The reference remains unclear without identifying whose side.
Arrows teach relationships, not technique suitability or permission.

weekly-kaigo-gap-anatomy-terms-probe.prompt: A note confuses scrotum and testes and says “pull” without identifying the target. Which correction is appropriate?
options: Distinguish outer scrotal sac, internal testes and foreskin over the glans; do not perform an unclear movement and ask professionals.
Nearby structures mean either name indicates the same action.
Knowing definitions establishes action target and method.
A written action means verified technique for others.
rationales: This distinguishes structures without using terminology to justify an unconfirmed action.
Outer sac and inner organs are separate despite proximity.
Definitions differ from checking the target and safe method.
Written mention is not safety verification; do not pass on ambiguous movements unchanged.

weekly-kaigo-depth-qol-outcome-probe.prompt: More albums were completed, but the person wanted time for photo memories. Which QOL evaluation is appropriate?
options: More albums establish greater satisfaction.
Exclude choice because assistance was needed.
Record quantity separately from experience and ask desired time use and roles to review support.
Since satisfaction is not externally certain, omit the person’s words.
rationales: Output alone does not establish satisfaction or purpose.
Assistance needs do not remove self-determination.
This distinguishes quantity from meaning and reviews through wishes.
Avoiding assumptions does not mean ignoring valuable personal evaluation.

weekly-kaigo-depth-community-choice-prob.prompt: A recorded-book listener wants to present at a community event, but staff limit presentation to independent print readers. What is appropriate?
options: Limit people needing support to listening regardless of wishes.
Ask preferred presentation and discuss preparation using experience and abilities.
A common venue removes checks of different participation methods.
Require identical reading ability before considering methods.
rationales: Support and contributing roles can coexist; check wishes.
This uses wishes and abilities to arrange participation.
Being present does not establish desired involvement.
One required method can exclude valuable experience and possibilities.

weekly-kaigo-depth-service-location-prob.prompt: Plans show 1 staff visiting home, 2 the person attending by day and returning home, 3 residential living. Which handoff is appropriate?
options: 1 day, 2 home visit, 3 residential; no date checks.
All have care staff, so settings need no distinction.
1 home, 2 day, 3 residential; names also establish fees and eligibility.
Distinguish 1 home visit, 2 day, 3 residential; check actual date, place and support separately.
rationales: Travel actors in 1 and 2 are reversed; category does not fix time.
Setting and living place matter beyond staff presence.
Categories alone do not establish personal eligibility or fees.
This separates provision forms and actual confirmed arrangements.

weekly-kaigo-depth-care-evaluation-probe.prompt: The goal is choosing an afternoon activity. After three explanations the person still says the choices are unclear. Which evaluation is appropriate?
options: Three explanations establish chosen-activity achievement.
The cause is certainly insufficient effort.
Separate explanation facts from unmet outcome and review explanation, conditions and goals with the person and team.
Record explanation counts and exclude responses.
rationales: Counts establish staff action, not an understood choice.
Unconfirmed explanations and conditions prevent blaming effort.
This distinguishes action and result and revisits suitable support.
Responses are central to evaluating goal-related effects.
